title: Routing & Auth Handoff — Surgical Sync notes 2026-04-07
content:
Rapid sync (20m) — surgical handoff focus
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 10:00–10:20 PT
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha, Marcus, Lena, Samir, Eliot (+ async notes from Nora)
Purpose: transfer ownership for two rolling items (quota counter durability & auth fallback) and align on a small set of runbook changes before next deploy window.

1) Quick wins / what shipped since last sync
- Deployed soft-fail for legacy token-introspect (auth) to canary region us-west-2; reduced 5xx from 0.7% -> 0.12% on canary. (owner: Marcus)
- Circuit-breaker tuning for routing goroutines merged, limits increased for short bursts (PR #987). Observed 8% better tail latency under spike load. (owner: Samir)
- Small quota-metrics cleanup: removed duplicate counter emitted by fallback path. Reduced cardinality in metrics pipeline. (owner: Lena)

2) Current priorities (top 3 for the week)
- Durable quota counters: design + checklist for switching to Redis Streams as write-ahead log to avoid lost increments during leader failover. Target: design review by 2026-04-12.
- Auth fallback policy: finalize SLA for token-introspect fallback vs. short-circuit local cache (tradeoff: security signal vs. latency). Target: policy approved by product on 2026-04-09.
- Routing fallthrough analytics: finish a 72-hour trace capture across p99 routes to quantify cost of cross-region fallthroughs. Target: 2026-04-10.

3) Blockers & escalations
- Capacity: Dedicated infra team flagged a GPU maintenance window 2026-04-11 that might affect our routing load generator. Need to confirm whether we can move the canary run to 2026-04-13. (escalation owner: Eliot)
- Redis Streams PoC: missing permission to provision namespace in staging (blocked by infra ticket INFRA-2109). Samir to follow up with Helen (infra eng).
- Product decision pending for auth fallback TTL (30s vs 5m). If product doesn't decide by tomorrow, we'll default to 60s for canary.

4) Incident recap (night of 2026-03-30) — short postmortem snippet
- Symptom: transient quota enforcement lag causing 429 spikes for 17 minutes across EU region. Root cause: double-snapshot race when leader lease rotated during high write pressure.
- Mitigation taken: rolled back snapshot write path and increased retry window.
- Followups: implement leader-safe write-ahead logging (see Durable quota counters priority). Added as P0->P1 depending on implementation timeline.

5) Experiment notes & metrics to watch
- Batch-size tuning experiment: change 'continuous-batch' window from 8ms -> 20ms in routing pool A for heavy small-requests workload. Expected: 12–18% token-cost reduction at p50 with <5% impact to p95 latency. Monitor: token-cost, p95 latency, tail requests failed. (Experiment ID: EXP-plat-2026-04-batch1)
- KV cache hit-rate probe: new probe deployed to staging to measure cold-start TTL effect. Metric: cache_hit_ratio_by_route (prometheus label route_id). Goal: achieve >85% hit for common routes.

6) Decisions made in this sync
- Default canary TTL for auth fallback: 60s (temporary), pending product signoff for 5m.
- Routing fallthrough logging sampling set to 10% for next 72 hours to avoid excessive cost while collecting signal.
- Move forward with Redis Streams PoC for quota durability; only enable WAL in staging for 2 weeks before prod ramp.

7) Action items (explicit owners & tickets)
- Samir: unblock INFRA-2109 + provision staging Redis Streams namespace (ETA 2026-04-09) -> LINEAR-PLT-543
- Lena: write runbook for auth fallback (include decision tree + escalation contacts) (ETA 2026-04-08) -> ENG-4321
- Marcus: schedule canary load run (if maintenance moves) and coordinate with SRE on noise windows (ETA 2026-04-09)
- Eliot: confirm infra maintenance window impact and propose alternative windows (ETA 2026-04-08)
- Aisha: consolidate experiment dashboard (EXP-plat-2026-04-batch1) and share readout template (ETA 2026-04-10)

8) Runbook & docs to update this week
- Quota counter design doc (Confluence) — append WAL migration checklist, update rollback instructions.
- Routing fallthrough playbook — add sampling config and cost estimate section.
- Auth fallback runbook — include an annotated decision table and monitoring thresholds.

9) Parking lot / unresolved questions
- If Redis Streams PoC shows >2x write amplification, fallback plan? Options: compacted counter with idempotent writes or shard-level lease window. Need micro-benchmark. (Samir to propose by 2026-04-12)
- Product to confirm attack model tradeoffs: is a 60s TTL acceptable for regulated customers? (Product/Compliance)

10) Quick sync checklist for next meeting
- Readout: sample of routing fallthrough trace + cost delta (owner: Marcus)
- PoC status: Redis Streams staging + metrics (owner: Samir)
- Auth TTL decision (owner: Product / Aisha to chase)

Appendix: quick heat map (team perception scores; 1 = low urgency, 5 = critical)
- Durable quota counters: 5
- Auth fallback policy: 4
- Routing fallthrough analytics: 3
- Batch tuning experiment: 2

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the experimental telemetry tags consistent across PRs (use exp_tag:plat-apr-batch1).
- Remind SRE to exclude fallthrough samples from monthly billing run for test accounts.
- We should consider a cross-team tabletop if quota durability becomes multi-region issue.

Next sync: 2026-04-09 10:00 PT (tentative)
